Prior to the bank’s collapse, Oliver Cowdery had been one of the earliest donors to the Book of Mormon translation and to the Church. In 1829 he gave part of his teacher’s salary to Joseph and Emma Smith for a down payment on a house in Harmony, Pennsylvania, where most of the translation occurred.
